subject: Prompt eval scope, prioritization, and escalation path
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: dev@atlasapps.com
Date: 2028-07-22 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt eval scope, prioritization, and escalation path

Team —

Quick sync item: AtlasApps is targeting a pilot in mid-August and has asked for a short, prioritized eval scope for the set of shopping assistant prompts we ship. I attached a preliminary scope and a prioritization matrix (prompt_suite_scope.xlsx / eval_prioritization_matrix.csv).

High-level asks:
- Define the minimal prompt subset for an initial A/B (canary) with AtlasApps (goal: detect regressions, validate responses across 3 intents).
- Agree acceptance criteria per prompt (latency, correctness thresholds, hallucination flags).
- Define escalation + rollback path if the canary exposes quality regressions.

Constraints to keep in mind: Dedicated capacity may be limited during their time window; we should be explicit about fallback model options.

I propose a short decision call today (30m) and to capture action owners in this thread.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachments: prompt_suite_scope.xlsx (sheet: prompts-to-test), eval_prioritization_matrix.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: dev@atlasapps.com
Date: 2028-07-22 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt eval scope, prioritization, and escalation path

On Jul 22, 2028, at 09:15, Jonas Weber wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick sync item: AtlasApps is targeting a pilot in mid-August and has asked for a short, prioritized eval scope for the set of shopping assistant prompts we ship.

Thanks Jonas — I reviewed the attachments. My product asks and proposed prioritization:

1) Minimal A/B scope (canary):
   - 12 prompts (4 core intents x 3 difficulty tiers). See tab "canary_set" in prompt_suite_scope.xlsx.
   - User-facing acceptance: >= 85% correctness on our annotation set; no high-severity hallucination incidents (as defined in section 3 of the matrix).

2) Metrics to surface during the canary:
   - Per-prompt semantic-accuracy (annotation agreement), token latency P95, and hallucination count.
   - A/B comparison will run for 48 hours with sampling at 5% traffic directed to canary variant.

3) Prioritization rationale:
   - Start with intents that impact revenue (checkout recommendations) then expansion intents. See priority column in eval_prioritization_matrix.csv.

Action items (proposed):
- Karthik: confirm feasibility for 5% continuous sampling and whether KV-cache priming affects latency baselines.
- Grace: propose test harness and annotation roster (ops + external annotators).
- Tessa: coordinate stakeholder comms and the pilot calendar with AtlasApps.

I can lead the acceptance criteria doc and consolidate the final matrix by EOD.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: dev@atlasapps.com
Date: 2028-07-22 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt eval scope, prioritization, and escalation path

On Jul 22, 2028, Marissa Cole wrote:
> Thanks Jonas — I reviewed the attachments. My product asks and proposed prioritization:

Quick technical notes / constraints:
- 5% sampling to canary variant is fine from a routing perspective but continuous sampling for 48h will require us to reserve a small Dedicated slot during the peak window to avoid tail latency spikes (I estimate a 0.8 GPU-day commit). If that slot isn't available we should default to a quantized CPU-compatible variant — I can prepare the compatible model build.
- KV-cache priming: the canary dataset must include warm-start sessions for the top 3 intents; otherwise P95 will be biased high. Please flag warm-start items in the prompt CSV.
- Acceptance criteria: I agree with >=85% annotation agreement, but suggest we add a rollback threshold that considers both quality and cost (example: if quality drops below 80% OR P95 latency increase >30% over baseline then trigger rollback).

I'll attach a short checklist in the drive (linked) with the model build tags we need.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, dev@atlasapps.com
Date: 2028-07-23 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt eval scope, prioritization, and escalation path

On Jul 22, 2028, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> Quick technical notes / constraints:

QA plan outline:
- Annotation roster: 6 internal annotators + 12 external (AtlasApps-provided) reviewers. Timeline: 48h labeling window after canary.
- Test harness: I'll reuse the lightweight harness from the NLU smoke suite and add per-prompt checkpoints. Output will include: prediction, confidence, annotation tag, and hallucination flag.
- Canary run and rollback: run canary at 5% traffic for 48h. If we hit rollback threshold (quality <80% OR P95 latency +30%) ops will:
   1) Pause canary routing.
   2) Re-route all traffic to the baseline model.
   3) Open an incident with SRE and product + attach evaluation artifacts (drive link).

I will own the test harness deliverable and the initial labeling rules doc. Marissa, I need your final acceptance text to include the hallucination severities so the annotators have binary flags and severity tiers.

-Grace
Grace O'Connor
QA Manager, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com

Date: 2028-07-24 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt eval scope, prioritization, and escalation path

Thanks all — good progress. Quick summary and escalation path (finalizing):

Decisions captured:
- Canary set: 12 prompts (Marissa).
- Acceptance: >=85% annotation agreement to pass; rollback if <80% OR latency P95 grows >30% (Karthik + Grace).
- Canary config: 5% traffic for 48h with warm-start sessions (Karthik).
- QA: 6 internal + 12 external annotators; harness owned by Grace.

Escalation path (if canary fails):
1) On detection, Grace or SRE pauses canary routing immediately.
2) Triage call (15m) with product+eng+SRE within 30 minutes.
3) If regression is model-specific and not quickly remediable, route to baseline and initiate regression incident runbook (I own escalation to leadership).

Next steps / owners:
- Marissa: finalize acceptance wording and send to Grace (EOD today).
- Karthik: confirm dedicated slot or quantized fallback by tomorrow AM.
- Grace: finalize harness + labeling rules by Friday.
- Tessa: lock pilot calendar with AtlasApps and share final window.

One-line approvals please ("approve" or "need changes") so I can mark this as green.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
